Messages.Author: Librarian
Messages.Body:
Hi LSJ -

We had a question about Kholos in our Release party tournament this
evening.

Ishtarri Kholo
React/ActMod
Only Usable during a Pol Act.
Usable by a tapped vampire. Title.
Put this card on this Ishtarri to represent the unique Laibon title of
Ishtarri Kholo (worth 2 Votes). Not usable if there are any older
ready untitled Ishtarri. Whenever this vampire is not a ready Ishtarri
or there is an older ready untitiled Ishtarri, move this card to (one
of) the oldest ready untitled Ishtarri (if any).

This card can be played during a referendum.

2 Questions:
Two different reacting Meths have the two oldest untitled Ishtarri.
They both attempt to play the card. What is the timing? Our specific
questions:
Do they contest before or after the votes are cast, and whichever it
is, what is the status of the cast votes, do they count or not?
Is it whomever says "I play the Ishtarri Kholo" first gets to vote?

Another scenario with Kholo: Someone else has the oldest Ishtarri Kholo
already in play. I have an Ishtarri the same age. The other Meth
votes with his Ishtarri Kholo. I then play my Ishtarri Kholo onto my
vampire. Do the votes from the other meth still stand?

As judge, I ruled that the Kholos would contest, and the any votes cast
by those Kholos would not count, regardless of when in the referendum
they were cast. But I had no real reason to do so, except for
smoothness and to prevent the "I played it first"/"I put it down on the
table first" sort of arguments...

best -

chris

Messages.Author: Gregory Stuart Pettigrew
Messages.Body:
On Wed, 15 Nov 2005, Librarian wrote:

> Hi LSJ -
>
> We had a question about Kholos in our Release party tournament this
> evening.
>
> Ishtarri Kholo
> React/ActMod
> Only Usable during a Pol Act.
> Usable by a tapped vampire. Title.
> Put this card on this Ishtarri to represent the unique Laibon title of
> Ishtarri Kholo (worth 2 Votes). Not usable if there are any older
> ready untitled Ishtarri. Whenever this vampire is not a ready Ishtarri
> or there is an older ready untitiled Ishtarri, move this card to (one
> of) the oldest ready untitled Ishtarri (if any).
>
> This card can be played during a referendum.
>
> 2 Questions:
> Two different reacting Meths have the two oldest untitled Ishtarri.
> They both attempt to play the card. What is the timing?

1.6.1.5. Ha, take that, LSJ.

> Do they contest before or after the votes are cast, and whichever it
> is, what is the status of the cast votes, do they count or not?

A vampire who loses votes during a referendum may lose votes he already
cast.

> Is it whomever says "I play the Ishtarri Kholo" first gets to vote?
>

Yes, and then when those votes are lost, they are no longer tallied.

> Another scenario with Kholo: Someone else has the oldest Ishtarri Kholo
> already in play. I have an Ishtarri the same age. The other Meth
> votes with his Ishtarri Kholo. I then play my Ishtarri Kholo onto my
> vampire. Do the votes from the other meth still stand?
>

No, that vampire no longer has any votes.

> As judge, I ruled that the Kholos would contest, and the any votes cast
> by those Kholos would not count, regardless of when in the referendum
> they were cast. But I had no real reason to do so, except for
> smoothness and to prevent the "I played it first"/"I put it down on the
> table first" sort of arguments...
>

No card in the game actually *subtracts* votes, but the rules for that
should intuitively follow gaining votes - when you gain the votes, you may
cast them, when you lose the votes, you cannot cast them.

--
- Gregory Stuart Pettigrew
